title: Todoist Review (2026)
intro: Todoist is evaluated here as a lightweight board / Kanban project tool — Todoist is a task and to-do manager for individuals and small teams with natural-language task capture, projects, labels, filters and light board/calendar views. Beginner Free; Pro ~$6.25/user/mo annual; Business ~$10/user/mo (plus local tax) with team workspace features. Strong for personal productivity and light team tasks — not a full Work OS. This review uses SoftwareGlimpse’s project-management methodology (ease of use, work planning, automation, collaboration, integrations, reporting, scalability, value, AI), scoring products inside their job cluster rather than against unrelated peers. It is based on first-party research, not hands-on lab testing.
summary: Choose Todoist when personal or light team task management is the job — landscape beside Work OS peers.
verdict: Choose Todoist when personal or light team task management is the job — landscape beside Work OS peers. Compare Asana/ClickUp for team Work OS, Trello for Kanban boards, and Motion for AI calendar auto-scheduling. Scores reflect first-party documentation as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing. Confirm current packaging, minimums and usage rates on the vendor site before purchase.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Best-in-class personal task capture UX — near-instant for individuals.
Projects/labels/filters — not portfolio/Gantt Work OS planning — 5 by design.
Light assists and recurring rules; far thinner than ClickUp/Asana.
Business team workspace helps; still weaker than Work OS collaboration suites.
90+ integrations narrative is strong for a task app.
Productivity visuals only — not manager dashboards.
Fine for individuals/small teams; not enterprise PMO scale.
Free + ~$6.25 Pro is excellent for the task-manager job. Affiliate economics excluded.
Todoist Assist features exist but are not Motion-class AI scheduling.

bestFor: Light team task lists on Business
limitations: Not a Work OS or portfolio tool
Reporting is personal productivity, not PMO

faq.question: Is Todoist a project management / work OS tool?
faq.answer: No. Todoist is an adjacent desktop workspace organizer. It wraps web apps into desktop shells — it is not a project tracker or work OS.

faq.question: How is Todoist priced?
faq.answer: Free Beginner; Pro ~$6.25, Business ~$10 per user/mo annual. Confirm live.

faq.question: Does Todoist have a free plan or free trial?
faq.answer: Yes — a free plan is published. A free trial is documented. Confirm current terms with the vendor.

faq.question: Did SoftwareGlimpse personally test Todoist?
faq.answer: No. This review is based on first-party product and pricing research evidence, not hands-on product usage. Affiliate relationships never influence scores.
